sources: v1.0, 15 Jul 2026 (incl. Figure 1 architecture and §11 persona journeys)
10 boards received 15 Oct 2026: ecosystem, 5-platform architecture, unified platform vision, end-user, community member, facility, academy & club, seller & brand, coach & expert, creator journeys
v2.1: WBS & Integrated Project Plan, Delivery Model, Technical Approach

conflicts.title: Single sign-on and in-app role switching
conflicts.vision: "One Login (SSO)" across all apps; a single "Super App" with a "Switch Role" screen (Player, Coach, Tournament Organiser, Venue Partner) (S3 boards 2–3)
conflicts.sow: SSO out of scope (§4). Two apps with separate logins; a person switches context by logging into the other app (§7). Figure 1: "two apps, one shared identity (no SSO)".
conflicts.impact: Determines app structure (one super-app vs User App + Partner App) and identity session design. Shared Identity (F3) goes live on 20 Oct on the SOW model.
conflicts.options: A) Keep SOW model for Phase 2 (no SSO, two apps). B) Add SSO across apps later (identity is OIDC-based, so this is mainly session configuration). C) Move to one super-app with in-app role switching (app restructure; change request).
conflicts.rec: A for Phase 2, with B kept open: F3 already uses one OIDC identity service, so SSO can be enabled later without rework. Treat C as a Stage-2 product decision with its own change request.

conflicts.title: Wallet with stored balance and partner "Withdraw"
conflicts.vision: "One Wallet … All transactions. One Balance" with a user balance (₹5,250); coaches and sellers see "Available Balance" with a "Withdraw" button (S3 boards 3, 8, 9)
conflicts.sow: No stored-value wallet, credits or float (§4). Transaction Ledger is read-only; funds route directly to partners via Razorpay Route so SportSeek never holds funds (§8.3).
conflicts.impact: Regulatory, not only functional: a balance usable to pay third-party partners is likely to fall under RBI prepaid payment instrument (PPI) rules; holding partner earnings for on-demand withdrawal risks the Payment Aggregator licensing the SOW is designed to avoid.
conflicts.options: A) Keep SOW model: Ledger view + Route settlements; show partners "earnings & settlement status", not a withdrawable balance. B) Wallet/balance through a licensed PPI issuer or bank partner (separate programme). C) Closed-loop reward points only (not money; see DEC-14).
conflicts.rec: A for Phase 2. Align vision artwork and marketing copy now. Any wallet (B) only after SportSeek legal/regulatory sign-off, as a separate change request.

conflicts.title: Timing of Community and Analytics
conflicts.vision: Phase 2 (0–6 months): Unified Identity & SSO, One Wallet, Role Management, Unified Notifications, Enhanced Partner App, Core Analytics, Community Module (S3 board 3)
conflicts.sow: Community and basic Analytics are Phase 2B, after the 2A "harden & unify" scope (§3.2, §12.1 M7–M8)
conflicts.impact: Expectation gap: Srivin plan completes 2A on 23 Mar 2027 with no community or analytics features. Stakeholders reading the vision roadmap may expect them by then.
conflicts.options: A) Keep SOW sequence; start 2B (Community + Expert Booking + basic analytics) on the same monthly train from Apr 2027. B) Pull a thin community slice (groups + feed + reviews) into 2A by swapping with a later 2A feature. C) Run a second pod in parallel from Jan 2027 (cost).
conflicts.rec: A, plus start event capture for analytics from R2 (G9) so dashboards are fast to deliver in 2B. Confirm the published roadmap with SportSeek stakeholders.

conflicts.title: Marketplace model (resolves SOW open item)
conflicts.vision: Third-party sellers and brands: onboarding, catalogue, orders, shipping, returns, payouts, promotions (S3 board 8)
conflicts.sow: Open item ⚑: "Is RA only showing data of the users or is it building a marketplace?" Build vs headless-commerce decision pending (§3.3)
conflicts.impact: The vision confirms a multi-seller marketplace. This brings e-commerce obligations (seller disclosures, returns, grievance handling) and marketplace tax treatment into scope for 2C.
conflicts.options: A) Custom build on the SportSeek platform. B) Headless commerce platform integrated via APIs. C) Partner marketplace integration.
conflicts.rec: Decide before 2C planning; Srivin to provide a build-vs-buy assessment in Q1 2027. No 2A impact.

gaps.title: Cache, object/media storage and search index missing from Srivin architecture
gaps.evidence: SOW Figure 1 shows Redis cache, object storage (media, docs) and a search index (future); vision shows "Content Storage", "Cache Layer", "Global Search" (S1, S3 board 2). Srivin TAD diagram shows only PostgreSQL and the analytics stream.
gaps.impact: Images, documents and KYC files have no designed home; global search across people, venues and events has no path; performance headroom for search and availability is reduced.
gaps.rec: Add Redis (cache, rate limits, OTP throttling), object storage + CDN (images, documents; signed URLs; restricted bucket for KYC), and a search ADR: PostgreSQL full-text/geo now, a dedicated search engine when global search ships.

gaps.title: No Organisation (business account) model in identity
gaps.evidence: Academies/clubs with coaches, staff and members; facilities with "staff & access management" and multiple venues; brands with teams (S3 boards 6–8)
gaps.impact: F3 models roles per person only. Without an Organisation entity, staff logins, multi-venue businesses and academy ERP (2C) force identity rework.
gaps.rec: Add Organisation, Membership and organisation-scoped roles (owner, manager, staff, coach) as an additive extension of the F3 identity schema. Partner services belong to an Organisation, not only a person.
gaps.when: Design: HLD (23 Oct). Build: R2 (additive; no change to R1).

gaps.title: Minors, guardians and children's data not modelled
gaps.evidence: U14/U15 athletes aged 14–17 (S3 boards 7, 9), school sports, academy "parent access" (S1 §11.5), with performance tracking, AI recommendations and ads in the vision
gaps.impact: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, processing a child's (under-18) personal data needs verifiable parental consent, and tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children are restricted. Identity goes live 20 Oct.
gaps.rec: Legal view before launch on whether under-18s may register on 20 Oct (interim age gate if needed). Then: date of birth / age capture, guardian linkage and consent records, exclusion of minors from targeted ads and profiling, guardian-managed accounts for academies.

gaps.title: No pricing, fee and commission engine
gaps.evidence: Commission bands (bookings 5–20%, marketplace 10–30%), per-session expert commission, coupons, packages, "boost visibility" (S3 board 2, 6, 8)
gaps.impact: Route split settlement, GST on SportSeek fees and the Ledger all need correct line items. Without an order/line-item model, F5 refunds, F9 Ledger and F11 payouts will compute amounts inconsistently.
gaps.rec: Introduce an order model with line items (price, discount, platform fee, taxes, partner share) and configurable fee rules per partner type/category; this drives Route splits, refunds and invoicing.
gaps.when: Design: by 13 Nov (before F5 build). Build: R3–R6.

gaps.title: No recurring payments / subscriptions
gaps.evidence: "Go Premium", monthly coaching programmes, facility memberships, seller plans, fan subscriptions (S3 boards 4, 6, 9, 10)
gaps.impact: Subscription revenue streams have no payment path; retrofitting mandates and renewals into the payments area later is costly.
gaps.rec: Reserve a Subscriptions capability in the payments area (gateway subscriptions / UPI AutoPay / e-mandate), with ledger events for renewals and failures.

gaps.title: Rewards and points need their own ledger
gaps.evidence: Points, XP, levels, badges, "Redeem points" for turf discounts and merchandise (S3 boards 5, 10)
gaps.impact: Mixing points with the Transaction Ledger blurs financial reporting and the no-stored-value position (C2).
gaps.rec: Separate double-entry Rewards ledger with expiry and redemption rules; redemptions appear in orders as discount line items (G4). Not money and not withdrawable.

gaps.title: No real-time channel
gaps.evidence: Live scores and match updates (S2 "real-time match engine"; S3), chat and messaging, live comments
gaps.impact: Polling does not scale for live tournaments or chat; adding real-time later touches mobile, web and back end.
gaps.rec: ADR for a real-time layer (SignalR within the .NET estate, or a managed real-time service), with fan-out sized for tournament peaks.

gaps.title: No in-app notification inbox
gaps.evidence: Vision Notification Engine lists "In-App" alongside Email, SMS, Push (S3 board 2)
gaps.impact: Users cannot review past alerts; push-only delivery is lossy.
gaps.rec: Add a notification centre (stored notifications, read/unread, deep links) to F4.

gaps.title: Data for analytics and AI not captured until 2B
gaps.evidence: Vision: Data Lake, Event Stream, Real-time Analytics, AI recommendations at 6–12 months (S3 board 2–3); SOW: AI needs 6–12 months of production data first (§3.3)
gaps.impact: If capture starts in 2B, the data needed for AI will not exist when 2C starts.
gaps.rec: From R2, stream domain events (with a documented, versioned event taxonomy and consent flags) to low-cost raw storage; build dashboards in 2B on top.

gaps.title: No public / partner API and integration strategy
gaps.evidence: "Open API Layer: connects partners, devices & third parties"; IoT-ready facility management; wearables (S3 board 4; S2 add-ons)
gaps.impact: Integrations get built ad hoc through internal APIs, which become hard to change.
gaps.rec: Separate partner API surface at the gateway: OAuth client credentials, API keys per partner, rate limits, versioning, outbound webhooks with signing.
gaps.when: Principle in HLD (23 Oct). Build: when first external integration is prioritised.

gaps.title: Partner-facing dashboards need multi-tenant analytics
gaps.evidence: Facility, coach, academy and seller dashboards with revenue, utilisation, demographics, forecasts, downloadable reports (S3 boards 6–9)
gaps.impact: "Buy a BI tool" (SOW §6.1) covers internal reporting; dashboards inside partner apps need per-partner row-level security and embedding.
gaps.rec: Choose an analytics tool that supports secure embedding and row-level security, or build partner dashboards from pre-aggregated tables.

gaps.title: No trust & safety or dispute capability
gaps.evidence: Verified profiles, content moderation, report & block, code of conduct, dispute resolution (S3 boards 5, 8)
gaps.impact: User-generated content and marketplace disputes carry legal duties (grievance handling under the IT Intermediary Rules and Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules).
gaps.rec: Moderation and disputes area: report queue, automated + human moderation, appeal flow, grievance officer workflow, audit trail.

gaps.title: International readiness basics
gaps.evidence: Phase 4: international payments, global tournaments, new sports (S3 board 3)
gaps.impact: International support is out of SOW scope (§4), but money without currency codes and local timestamps are very costly to retrofit.
gaps.rec: Store ISO 4217 currency with every amount, timestamps in UTC with venue time zone, translatable strings, locale-aware formatting. No multi-currency features in Phase 2.
gaps.when: Principle in HLD (23 Oct); applied from R2.

gaps.title: Media and streaming platform
gaps.evidence: Live streaming, highlights, reels, creator content, copyright protection, ads (S3 boards 1, 10)
gaps.impact: Out of SOW scope (§4) but central to the vision's 5th platform.
gaps.rec: Reserve a Media area boundary; use a managed video service (upload, transcode, CDN, DRM) when scoped. Images and short media use G1 storage meanwhile.

gaps.title: Smaller vision items not in any plan
gaps.evidence: Calendar sync (S2, S3 board 6), video sessions with experts (S2, S3 board 9), shipping & returns (S2, S3 board 8), referral and affiliate tracking (S3 boards 6, 10), guest browsing (S3 board 4)
gaps.impact: Each is small, but together they shape stakeholder expectations.
gaps.rec: Log as backlog epics with phase tags; guest browsing and calendar export can ride an early 2B train.
